featured_reviews.name: Note from Travelam
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had an amazing experience with Mumbai Dream Tours! A special thanks to Hardhik, who made this journey truly memorable with his incredible knowledge, guidance, and hospitality throughout the tour.

The 3-hour trek was one of the most unique experiences in Mumbai, covering iconic places like the world’s largest open-air laundry at Dhobi Ghat, the fascinating Dabbawala system, and the vibrant life of Dharavi. Hardhik explained every detail with so much passion and insight, making the entire experience engaging and meaningful.

What stood out the most was how comfortable and well-guided we felt throughout the tour. It was not just sightseeing, but a real understanding of Mumbai’s culture, people, and hardworking spirit.

Highly recommended for anyone visiting Mumbai and wanting to explore the city beyond the usual tourist spots. Thank you once again, Hardhik and Mumbai Dream Tours, for such a wonderful experience!

featured_reviews.name: Danna Katzman
featured_reviews.review_text: We went on the Dharavi Slum Tour with Rakesh as our guide. It was intense, overwhelming, and inspiring all at once. Rakesh was wonderful - very knowledgeable and willing to answer all our many questions. He took us through the bustling commercial area first and then we also saw a crowded residential area. This tour really makes you think about ones own privilege, the ways many people in this world have to live, and the how they find opportunities to thrive. Highly recommend this tour.

featured_reviews.name: Felicitas
featured_reviews.review_text:
The tour with Abhi was one of the absolute highlights of my time in Mumbai: insightful, respectful and so much more than a typical city tour. Abhi guides you through Dhobi Ghat and Dharavi with calmness and authenticity, explains social and economic contexts, shares stories from the community and manages to convey a complex reality. I learned so many new things!
Also I felt safe and well taken care of at all times, and the tour genuinely moved me. If you’re looking for a tour that not only provides information but also real insight and connection, Abhi is the perfect guide.

Mumbai Heritage Walk: Where Old Bombay Still Runs the Show

Most tourists photograph Mumbai's skyline and move on. Smart travellers walk it instead. Two hours on foot through South Mumbai teaches you more than a week of taxi windows ever could.

What the Walk Actually Covers

The Mumbai Heritage Walk by Cityscape Mumbai Tours starts at Regal Cinema in Colaba and ends at Churchgate Station. In between, you pass 13 landmarks: the Gateway of India, the Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus, Rajabai Clock Tower, Flora Fountain, and more. Group tours run three times daily, and a local guide narrates the whole route in English.

The BMC Building: Old Bombay's Silent Boss

One landmark rarely gets the spotlight it deserves: the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation building. It sits directly opposite CST, and its 255-foot Gothic tower has quietly run Mumbai's water, roads, and waste systems since 1893. No ribbon-cutting ceremony ever matched this building's day job.

On the heritage walk, guides point out its honey-colored stone, the winged figure on its gable, and the statue of Sir Pherozeshah Mehta standing guard outside. It is easy to walk past a government office. It is hard to walk past this one.

Why Walk It With a Guide

Buildings do not explain themselves. A guide connects the dots between colonial ambition, Indian pride, and everyday civic grind, all in one two-hour loop. Prices start at ₹1,850 for adults; kids under 6 walk free.

featured_reviews.name: RuSo
featured_reviews.review_text: Sion Fort is a small but historically important spot tucked away in the busy heart of Mumbai. Built by the British in the 17th century, the fort sits on a hillock and once served as a watchtower to keep an eye on the surrounding areas. Today, it has been converted into a peaceful garden maintained by the BMC, making it a nice place for a short walk or some quiet time away from traffic and crowds. The fort structure itself is quite simple and not very well preserved, but the greenery and calm atmosphere make it pleasant to visit. It’s ideal for locals, morning walkers, and history enthusiasts looking for a quick, relaxed stop rather than a major tourist attraction.

featured_reviews.name: shailesh kathirvel
featured_reviews.review_text: Sion Fort is a peaceful little escape in the middle of the city. The climb is easy and takes just a few minutes, and once you reach the top, the view of Sion and the surrounding areas is really refreshing. It’s a great spot for a quick morning or evening visit, especially if you enjoy calm places and a bit of history. The fort is simple but well maintained, and the greenery around adds to the charm. A nice place to relax, walk around, and enjoy the breeze.

featured_reviews.name: INDERJIT BARAI
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sion Fort is a beautiful historical monument with great potential, but unfortunately, its condition has deteriorated due to irresponsible behavior by some visitors. The structure itself is impressive, and the fort still carries a strong historical charm with its old walls, arches, and scenic surroundings. If properly cared for, it could be an excellent heritage spot in the city.

However, the experience is spoiled by the actions of people who do not respect the monument. Names are scribbled on the walls, which damages the heritage value of the fort. It is also disturbing to see small boys around 8–10 years old smoking and using vapes inside the premises. Some reckless visitors pluck flowers and even climb on the fort walls, which are already weak and not in a safe condition. Such activities not only harm the monument but also put lives at risk. Overall, Sion Fort is a very good monument, but stricter rules, better maintenance, and public awareness are urgently needed to protect it for future generations.

featured_reviews.name: Learn 'To be smart
featured_reviews.review_text: Shiv Fort is a historical monument located in Sion, Mumbai. It is a good place to visit if you are interested in history, culture, and nature. The fort is situated on a hill, so you will have to climb many stairs to reach the top. The management is good and the stairs are well-maintained, but be prepared to get tired. There are different types of things you can buy on the way, such as souvenirs, snacks, and drinks. The view from the top is amazing, especially during sunset. You can take some awesome pictures and enjoy the scenery. However, there is not much to do on the top, so you might get bored if you do not bring enough food and entertainment. There is a park nearby for children, where they can play on the swings and other rides. To reach Shiv Fort, you can take a train to Sion station and then walk straight for about 600 meters. You will find the fort on the left side of the road. Overall, Shiv Fort is a nice place to visit for a day trip, but not very exciting if you are looking for more adventure.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. featured_reviews.review_text:
WHY SHOULD ONE GO TO SION FORT?
SIon fort has lot to offer
1) for locals - a get together spot in lap of nature to do yoga, walk, exercise like climbing running etc.
2) for mumbaikar - an unknown heritage site which gives you a peak into ancient architecture and impress your guest from outside the city
3) for visitor to Mumbai - not to be missed by heritage lovers, as it has remains of a fort - a canon , multiple dilapidated rooms, a possible water tank
for all of above, the views from Sion fort of Mumbai landscape is going to stun you. You can view the 360 degree Mumbai skyline from Navi Mumbai to Bandra Worli Sealink to Thane Bhandup creek all from one spot. Undoubtedly Sunrise and Sunset are worth the visit.
The place is restored and made into a open gym with various equipment's provided (Kudos to BMC) , landscaped garden, Rest rooms, filtered water provision and jogging trail
I was here for first time on 25 feb 2024 and should have been here much earlier in my life is what I were my first thoughts. I walked down with 7 kg backpack as practice to my big climb coming up & it was worth my time as it has a share of small trek as well.
This place has some surprisingly beautiful spots for photo shoots. (See my video till end)

HOW TO REACH
Located at Sion East. 15 minutes walk from Sion station on central Mumbai local railway line, 30 minutes walk from Chunnabhati stataion on Harbour Mumbai local railway line . You can take taxi at almost minimum fares from both railway station. There is enough provision for parking for private vehicles
Multiple  BEST BUSES including AC BUSES also stop near this place. Ask for Sion fort or sion east station bus stop
